annotation.title_clean: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: WHO guidance
annotation.title_en: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: WHO guidance
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: WHO guidance, developed by a 20-member expert group, setting six consensus ethical principles for AI in health and analysing ethical challenges, liability regimes and governance of data, the private and public sectors, regulation and global AI governance. It offers recommendations to governments, developers and providers. Robotics appears only in passing.
key_provisions_or_claims: Six principles: protect autonomy; promote well-being, safety and public interest; ensure transparency and explainability; foster responsibility and accountability; ensure inclusiveness and equity; promote responsive and sustainable AI.
Governments should require impact assessments, independent audits and transparent procurement standards for health AI.
Liability regimes should be updated; no-fault compensation funds and insurance are suggested.
Regulators should require prospective testing and post-market surveillance to detect bias, and consider licensing for high-risk AI.
Calls for WHO model legislation, a policy observatory and coordinated global governance with OECD, UNESCO and the Council of Europe.
